It has to do with a fundamental understanding of how we all think about eating. On a visceral, instinctive level. The one thing I've noticed across the board is that the response from fats toward healthy people AND from healthy people toward fats, is exactly the same, just in a different direction. When fats hear a healthy person describe their diet, it's always "How can they starve themselves?!" When healthy people hear how fats eat, it's almost disbelief, like they know it's happening around them everyday, but it's still so far fetched that anyone could be so greedy as to put THAT many calories into their bodies over the course of a day. Both are responding from an instinctive, primal place. How can they do that?! The reason for this is everyone, **everyone** is eating food the way their body is telling them to. The way they've always done. We are doing what is natural, what we are meant to do. Some of us are doing it differently, and we **think** that we're doing it the same, because we're using all the same language to describe it. "Eat until you're full, then stop." or eat X number of times per day. Both healthy and fat people can do these things, but do they them completely differently.

I've spent most of my adult life as a fat. Was never greed or dramatic overeating, it was because when i got out of high school, I spent about a year going to college in the morning and working full time at night. I spent a year where the only meal I ate was lunch. I'd get up, go to school, have about an hour downtime in between school and work to eat, then go to work and go right to sleep when done working. So I trained my body to become used to getting all of my caloric intake during one meal. This will absolutely make you gain fat. Guaranteed, across the board. Over the course of the next decade I would occasionally look into health information, not really seriously, the "healthy lifestyle" wasn't for me, and I knew it. But just as a mild curiosity. I would dabble here and there with healthy foods, never really "dieting" but gradually including things in my diet that most unhealthy people shy away from and healthy people embrace. I have no problem with fresh spinach, or any number of "healthy" produce items most fats shy away from because "ew, health food." I'm well aware that most of the health food is just as tasty as unhealthy food it's just different. I've spent a week or two at a time eating nothing but healthy food, but never really sticking with it. It wasn't really lack of self control or discipline or anything like that, I just listen to my body and give it what it wants. Now, I've recently lost a bunch of weight. Prolly 50 pounds in the last year, almost perfect weight loss from the getting in shape perspective. But the entire time I haven't stopped listening to my body, I've been giving it what it wants for the most part, the same as any other time in my life. Now I'm nowhere near shitlord status, but I know I'm going to be there one day. It's prolly a year or two off, but I know it'll happen. What I think happened, is a fundamental shift in the WAY I'm eating. I'm eating multiple times a day. Now I know what you're thinkin "duh, everyone does." but they don't all do it the same way. Fat people are not so much governed by number of meals per day as they are governed by what I'm going to call satiety inducing events. Now healthy people feel satiety after every meal, as they should, it's natural. Fat people tend to have 1-2 satiety inducing events in a given day, and everything else is considered inconsequential. If it doesn't induce satiety, it's "not a meal". This is why they are able to eat so many more calories than healthy people, it doesn't even register on the meal radar, because it doesn't induce satiety, so it couldn't possibly be that important. Everything else is just meaningless, trivial caloric intake. When fats hear that they need total calorie reduction or portion control, what they hear is the one "real" meal they get per day has to not be satisfying. This just feels wrong to them. Why would you not eat when your body tells you to?! Most of them skip breakfast, then maybe have a light lunch and then eat all their calories at night. They have trivial meaningless caloric intake throughout the day, if any, and then 1-2 satiety inducing events. The thing is, whether they have the caloric intake throughout the day or not, it's the satiety inducing events that are gaining the weight. the calories thru the day just speed the process up, that's all.
